Ling 285
    Exam 1 Review, Questions will be answered in Tuesday 9/29 Class


1. What’s the similarity between “m” in “mad” and “b” in “bad”, and what’s
   the difference between those sounds?

2. What’s the role of the learning rate in Stochastic Gradient Descent and the
   role of stiffness in (viscous) springy systems? What happens when learning
   rate is high vs. low and when stiffness is high vs. low?





3. What’s the physical principle behind how your auditory system hears
   different frequencies? Describe the basic physics of the basilar membrane
   to illustrate how the system works.




4. Imagine the following two temperature control systems, if you set the
   temperature at 70: a) Excellent thermostat right near the Air
   conditioning/Heating Unit: If the temperature is higher than 70, the AC
   turns on and temperature goes down to 70 and stays there, as the
   thermostat detects the right temperature and stops the AC. If the
   temperature were lower than 70, heating turns on till it gets to 70, and
   thermostat turns it off as it detects the right temperature. b) Thermostat
   really far from the AC/HU: If the temperature is higher than 70, the AC
   turns on and temperature goes down to 70, but the thermostat doesn’t
   detect that and the temperature keeps dropping till 60, and when the
   thermostat finally detects 60, it turns on HU, and heat comes on, and
   temperature rises to 70, but thermostat doesn’t detect it, till the
   temperature goes up to 80, etc. Which of these systems is like a spring by
    itself, and which is like a mass-spring?
